1.why: The reset token is stored on the server-side recovery session and `verify-token` compares the submitted token only against `session.resetToken`, so it is bound to the requesting browser session (though there is no real user account record).

2.why: A token is only accepted within the session that generated it (`session.resetToken` + timingSafeEqual), so a code from one session cannot be reused by another, making this statement false of the system.

3.why: Nothing invalidates or rotates the session ID/cookie after `reset-password`; the same pre-reset session continues on to `signin`/`authenticated`, so pre-existing sessions remain valid.

4.why: The server refuses to start without certs, serves only TLS on 3000, 308-redirects plaintext traffic and sets HSTS, but no explicit minimum TLS version (e.g. TLS 1.3) is configured, relying on Bun defaults.

5.why: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt (cost 10) and tokens come from `crypto.getRandomValues`, but reset tokens/MFA codes are kept in memory in plaintext and returned to the client, so they are not protected at rest.

6.why: There is no email delivery at all — delivery is simulated and the reset token and MFA code are echoed back in the API response and printed into the visible 'Logs' panel rather than guarded.

7.why: All inputs are strictly validated (allow-list regex for account, `/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{32,128}$/` for tokens, `/^[0-9]{6}$/` for MFA, length/complexity checks for passwords) and JSON-only bodies are parsed.

8.why: The only redirect is a hard-coded 308 to `https://localhost:3000/`; no user-controlled URL is ever used in a Location header or link.

9.why: No email templates exist, and the HTML page interpolates only a server-generated nonce while the client builds DOM exclusively via `textContent`/`createElement` under a strict nonce-based CSP.

10.why: `log()` writes the reset token and MFA code to `console.log` and to the on-page Logs panel ('Test reset token: …', 'Test MFA code: …'), so secrets are shown in logs.

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed and never logged, but the MFA code `"482913"` is hard-coded directly in the source, and TLS key paths/secret values are embedded rather than externalised.

12.why: There is no login with default username/password, but the static hard-coded MFA value `482913` functions as a default, predictable credential for every session.

13.why: `failedAttempt`/`isBlocked` lock each action for 60 s after 5 failures with a generic 429, though the counters are per-session so an attacker can reset them by discarding the cookie.

14.why: `recover` always returns the same neutral message ('If the account can be recovered, instructions…') regardless of input validity, and no account lookup or differing status is exposed.

15.why: The reset token is 32 bytes from `crypto.getRandomValues` encoded base64url, single-use (`resetUsed`), 10-minute TTL, and unique to the individual session.
